configs.description: The chassis with two AC supplies and two fan modules fitted, front-to-rear air, before any part number: the shape every build below starts from.
configs.name: base

configs.description: Two DC supplies and front-to-rear air: PWR-511-DC-RED supplies and FAN-7011M-F fan modules. The data sheet lists no DC part number for the switch; the supplies are spares, and a DC build is ordered through the "#" configurable SKU.
configs.name: dc-f

configs.description: Two DC supplies and rear-to-front air: PWR-511-DC-BLUE supplies and FAN-7011M-R fan modules. No DC part number is listed for the switch.
configs.name: dc-r

configs.description: The 7050SX3-48YC8 with two AC supplies and front-to-rear air: PWR-511-AC-RED supplies and FAN-7011M-F fan modules, all with red handles. Ordered as DCS-7050SX3-48YC8-F.
configs.name: f

configs.description: The 7050SX3-48YC8 with two AC supplies and rear-to-front air: PWR-511-AC-BLUE supplies and FAN-7011M-R fan modules, all with blue handles. Ordered as DCS-7050SX3-48YC8-R.
configs.name: r

gaps.note: Guide Table 4 prints 165 W typical and 345 W maximum for the 7050SX3-48YC8; the data sheet prints 124W / 301W for the same measure (typical at 25 C, 50 percent load, excluding transceivers; the guide gives no conditions). The guide's are modelled, as the newer of the two documents for what it prints.
gaps.wanted: the maker's statement of which is current.

gaps.note: Storage temperature -25 to 70 C (guide Table 2) against -40 to 70 C (data sheet). The guide's is in attrs.
gaps.wanted: the maker's statement of which is current.

gaps.note: The guide draws four generic rear panels (Figures D-1 to D-4) and does not say which model uses which. The 7050SX3-48YC8 is mapped to D-3 by its fan count (two, data sheet), its two supplies and its rear management ports. The data sheet's "Rear View" photograph (PDF page 3) for the 7050SX3-48YC8 and its siblings shows the same shape but is a thumbnail.
gaps.wanted: the maker's statement of the rear panel of the 7050SX3-48YC8.

gaps.note: The guide's Figures 3-1 to 3-14 are isometric drawings with no measure and the kit guides for KIT-7001, KIT-7101 and the other spares are not held, so no ear position or rail kit is written.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned drawing of the mounting bracket position, and the kit guides.

gaps.note: Figure C-15 draws four dots a QSFP port, but the guide's Appendix A describes one port LED and does not say what each of the four shows. All four are given the same states.
gaps.wanted: the guide's account of the port lamps, or a photograph of the lit face.

gaps.note: Figure C-15 draws two lamps under each SFP column. Which belongs to the upper port and which to the lower is not stated; the odd port is given the left lamp.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the lit face.

gaps.note: The speed bands' legends, the small print over the cages, the system and fan lamp glyphs and the PS1 and PS2 legends are unreadable or barely readable in the 576 px figure. The glyphs and the two PS legends are drawn as read; the band and cage legends are not drawn.
Which side the latches of the stacked cages face is not visible in the figure. The library's belly-to-belly convention is used (upper cage upright, lower turned 180).
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the stacked cages.

gaps.note: The management block's console symbol is drawn as the 7280SR3-48YC8 draws it; the figure's 1.26 px/mm resolves the block only as three stacked ports.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the rear management block.

gaps.note: The guide's Figure D-3 draws one generic supply; the PWR-511-AC and PWR-511-DC components are the library's, drawn from the 7280 guide's figure. The PWR-511-DC is the AC housing with a plain two-pole terminal block; the guide shows a DC supply only in isometric figures.
gaps.wanted: a flat drawing or photograph of the PWR-511-AC and PWR-511-DC.

gaps.note: The guide's power tables and the data sheet give whole-switch figures only; the fan modules' missing power figure (lint L27) stands. The supplies state their output.
Guide Table 5 gives the 7050SX3-48YC8 KIT-GND-EXT-1RU, attached on the bottom of the chassis (Figures 4-3 and 4-4). No flat figure measures a grounding point, so none is placed.
gaps.wanted: a flat drawing of the bottom with the grounding adapter holes.

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

chassis.note: Guide Table 1: 48.3 x 4.4 x 46.8 cm (19 x 1.75 x 18.43 inches), 9.5 kg (21.0 lbs); its footnote gives the depth as 50.5 cm (19.9 inches) with the power supplies and fans. Data sheet: 44 x 4.4 x 46.8 cm, 21 lbs (9.45 kg). The width: 48.3 cm is over the mounting ears, so the body between them, which is what is modelled, is the data sheet's 44 cm (440.0 here). The height is 43.7, as the library's other 7050 devices (the 4.4 cm of both documents is the 1RU rounding). The depth is the 46.8 cm both documents give (468.0), the body without the supplies' and fans' handles. The two weights are one weight to a rounding of 9.45 kg to one place. 1RU.

colour.note: The front plate is the median of the grey pixels (neither black nor white, low saturation) of the guide's figure C-15, #717274. The figure is a raster and its lighting is not known, so the shade is estimated.

configurations.note: Data sheet ordering information: DCS-7050SX3-48YC8-F and -R ("front-to-rear air, 2xAC" and "rear-to-front air, 2xAC"). The "#" SKU ("configurable fans and psu") is an order of parts, not a part number a DCIM can hold, and is not listed. The data sheet lists no DC build of the switch: the PWR-511-DC-RED and -BLUE supplies are spares, so the DC configurations are examples with no part number. The guide's Table 4 lists PWR-511-AC and PWR-511-DC as the supported supplies.

ears.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide's Chapter 3 mounts the switch with the accessory-kit brackets and shows them in isometric drawings that carry no measure. The data sheet lists the spares KIT-7001, KIT-7101, KIT-2POST-1U-NT, KIT-4POST-NT and KIT-GND-EXT-1U. No figure measures a bracket position, and the kit guides are not held, so no ear position is written and no rail kit is listed in chassis.kits. Recorded in the gap rack-ears.

environment.note: Guide Table 2: operating 0 to 40 C, storage -25 to 70 C, altitude 0 to 3,000 m, humidity 5 to 90 percent non-condensing. Data sheet: operating 0 to 40 C, storage -40 to 70 C, humidity 5 to 90 percent, altitude 0 to 3,000 m. The storage temperature differs: gap `environment`, the guide's used.

front-legend.note: The figure prints the maker's wordmark and the model line at the top left. THE WORDMARK IS NOT DRAWN: a logo-zone region is reserved over it and the plain model text is set.

front-ports.note: Figure C-15 at about 1.27 px/mm. Forty-eight SFP cages in two stacked rows (ports 1 to 48), twelve columns on each side of the QSFP block, in groups of six columns on a 14.25 mm pitch (the registry's ganged-SFP pitch, whose cages abut; the figure reads 13.9) with a 2.5 mm gap between the groups of six; ports 25 to 47 start 260.0 mm from the left. Eight QSFP100 cages in two stacked rows of four columns (49 to 56), centred 190.7, 209.6, 228.6 and 247.4 mm, a 19.0 mm pitch. The rows read at 18.1 and 31.9 mm down, a row pitch of 13.8. The belly-to-belly orientation is the library's convention (upper cage upright, lower turned 180); the figure is too small to show the latch side.

fru-bays.note: Guide Appendix E (E.2 power supplies, E.3 fan modules) gives removal and installation procedures, and the data sheet calls the supplies "1+1 hot-swappable". SO THE TWO POWER SUPPLIES AND THE TWO FAN MODULES ARE BAYS. Nothing on this chassis is a built-in unit. The management block, the USB port and the console port are part of the chassis and are placements.

gate-1-front.note: Figure C-15 passes. The raster is 576 x 159 pixels; the body between its plate edges measures about 560 px wide and 57 px tall (aspect 9.9) against the data sheet's 440 / 43.7 = 10.07, so the figure is near-orthographic and carries geometry at about 1.27 px/mm (the 440 mm body is the scale anchor; the dark stubs at the two ends are the ears and are not counted). One pixel is 0.8 mm, so every position is good to about 1 mm, and every one is `estimated` because it is read off a picture and no dimension states it. The figure is the same drawing as Figure C-6 of the 7280R3 Series guide for the 7280SR3-48YC8 (the same two rows of twenty-four SFP cages, the same eight QSFP cages between them): the positions of arista/7280sr3-48yc8 were read off C-15 at ports 1 and 49 (tab centres 10.8 and 190.6 mm against that device's 11.4 and 190.7) and agree to 0.6 mm, so they are used.

gate-1-rear.note: Figure D-3 is a 553 x 120 px raster whose chassis is 553 px between its edges (1.257 px/mm over the 440 mm body); positions are good to about 0.8 mm. The guide draws the rear generically (D-1 to D-4) and does not say which model uses which. The 7050SX3-48YC8 is mapped to D-3 by its two fan modules (data sheet: "Hot-swappable Fans 2 (1+1 redundant)"), its 1RU height, its two power supplies and its management ports at the rear (Figure C-15 has none at the front). The data sheet (PDF page 3) captions one rear photograph for the 7050SX3-48YC8 and its siblings, two fan modules with a plate between, which agrees; the guide does not name the figure, so THE MAPPING IS ESTIMATED. The two red fan modules read 79 mm wide at 105.8 and 275 mm across, as arista/7280sr3-48yc8 draws them.

interface-names.note: Not printed and not modelled. EOS names ports Ethernet1 to Ethernet56 and Management1; this is the vendor's convention and no held document prints it.

lifecycle.note: Searched the held documents (the guide and the data sheet) for an end-of-sale or end-of-life notice for the 7050SX3-48YC8: none. No web search was made, so this is a statement about those documents only.

other-faces.note: No source draws the top, bottom or sides flat. The guide's installation figures are isometric. Each carries an `empty` sentence. The guide's Table 5 gives this model KIT-GND-EXT-1RU on the bottom of the chassis (sections 4.1 and 4.2, Figures 4-3 and 4-4, a grounding adapter assembly); no figure measures it.

port-lamps.note: Guide Appendix A.1.2: each SFP column has two small green lamps in the strip under the lower row and each QSFP column a group of four above the upper cage and four below the lower one (Figure C-15). They are modelled as one lamp for each port of an SFP column, the odd port's on the left, and four lamps a QSFP port, as arista/7280sr3-48yc8 models the same drawing. Which lamp names which port, and what each of four QSFP lamps means, are the gaps sfp-lamp-pairing and port-lamp-count.

port-numbering.note: Figure C-15 (callout 5, "Port numbers") prints 1 over 2, 3 over 4, and so on, 1 to 48 across the SFP columns and 49 over 50 to 55 over 56 across the QSFP columns, which sit between ports 24 and 25 in space and are numbered after 48. The odd number is the upper cage. The figure prints each number on a white tab over the cage opening; a seated cage hides what is painted under it, so the numerals are set in the band between the two rows, the odd number left of its column centre and the even one right of it. EOS interface names are not printed on the metal and are not modelled.

power.note: Guide Table 4: typical / maximum 165 W / 345 W for the 7050SX3-48YC8 with PWR-511-AC or PWR-511-DC. The data sheet prints 124W / 301W, typical "measured at 25C ambient with 50% load on all ports, excludes transceivers". The guide's are modelled and the data sheet's are in the gap `power`; the two are the same measure, so this is a conflict. The guide does not state the conditions of its figures.

rear.note: Figure D-3 at 1.257 px/mm, the rear seen from behind with x = 0 at the left of the drawing. PS1 is the left and PS2 the right (callouts 1 and 6). Each power supply module is 73.5 mm wide (the data sheet's "73.5mm" for the PWR-511) at 4.4 and 361.5 mm across and 1.85 mm down; the figure draws the fan guard at the left of each supply and the C14 inlet at its right. The management block is a grey plate 82.5 to 100.5 mm across with the Ethernet management port, the USB port and the RJ-45 console port stacked in it. Two fan modules 78.6 mm wide at 105.7 and 276.6 mm across and 2.55 mm down, red frames with a honeycomb grille, a grey release rail and a status lamp at the bottom. Between the fans is a grey plate printed with ASSY NUMBER, SERIAL NUMBER and MAC ADDRESS fields and, under them, PS1 and PS2 legends beside airflow arrows (the arrows are not drawn). The positions are as arista/7280sr3-48yc8, whose figure is the same drawing.

rear-fan.note: Data sheet: "Hot-swappable Fans 2 (1+1 redundant)", "Fan Tray FAN-7011M-F/R" and the spares FAN-7011M-F (front-to-rear) and FAN-7011M-R (rear-to-front). Guide section 2.1: a red handle is an air-exit module and a blue handle an air-inlet one, and every module must have the same direction. The two fan modules are bays that accept FAN-7011M-F or -R; the -R configurations seat the blue modules. The components are the ones the 7280SR3-48YC8 seats: the maker's part number is the same, so the component is reused.

sources.note: 7050 Series 1RU (Gen 3) Quick Start Guide, Arista Networks, document DOC-00141-08, 57 pages, copyright 2025, PDF created 2025-08-19 (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/qsg/qsg-books/QS_7050_1RU_Gen3.pdf): Table 1 (dimensions and weights), Table 2 (operating and storage), Table 3 (power input), Table 4 (power draw and supported supplies), section 2.1 (airflow orientation, handle colour), section 4.1 and Table 5 (grounding), Appendix C (Figure C-15, the front panel of the DCS-7050SX3-48YC8), Appendix D (Figure D-3, the rear panel with management ports in the rear and two dual-fan modules), Appendix E (field replacement). 7050X3 Series 10/25/40/50/100G Data Center Switches Data Sheet, Arista Networks, 03-0040-46 (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/Datasheets/7050X3-Datasheet.pdf): the model comparison, the power supply specifications and the ordering information. Held and checked first: intake COVERAGE.md and SOURCES.md, which list no photograph, 3D model or CAD file for this model (Arista publishes none; a `find` of the intake folder for 3D files found none) and a Visio stencil master that was not used. No drawing, photograph or logo is copied into the library, only transcribed facts and new drawings.

speed-strips.note: Figure C-15 draws a cyan band between the two rows under each group of six SFP columns and a lavender band under the QSFP block, with tiny legends. The bands are drawn in those colours at 23.9 to 25.9 mm down; the legends are unreadable and are not drawn. Two brass-coloured screw heads sit at the ends of the QSFP lamp strip.

status-lamps.note: Figure C-15 callouts 1 to 4: a system status lamp, a fan status lamp and a status lamp for each of the two power supplies, in a row at the top right with a symbol or legend above each; the guide's Appendix A.1.1 states the colours. Four lamps at 419.1, 422.8, 426.9 and 431.1 mm across and 5.2 mm down, as arista/7280sr3-48yc8. The order (system, fan, PS1, PS2) is the callout order of the figure.

vents.note: The figure shows a perforated grid along the top in four fields, with solid strips between them and over the QSFP block, and a row of tiny holes along the bottom lip. Each field is drawn in its measured extent, as arista/7280sr3-48yc8; the individual squares are not drawn one by one.
